column1: # Label cleaning, layer 1, cleaning version 3: dose units after a digit (cleaning plan v7 "Dose units after a digit";
# training/cleaning.py). "written<TAB>abbreviation": a written form directly after a number token (digits with optional
# thousands commas and a decimal part, or a hyphenated range of two such numbers), separated by one space or, as an
# adjective, a hyphen ("10-milligram"), becomes " " + its abbreviation, written exactly as listed (the capitalization
# rule does not apply). Matched case-insensitively on whole tokens, longest first, so other casings of an abbreviation
# ("MG", "ml") take the listed casing and a plural abbreviation ("mgs") becomes singular. "<number> <unit> per <unit>",
# both units listed here, becomes "<number> <abbr>/<abbr>" ("5 milligrams per kilogram" -> "5 mg/kg").
# Left as written: a unit after a number word or without a number; "units" (never "U" or "IU": the Joint Commission's
# do-not-use list), "cc", grams and every non-medical unit; "percent" (the normalizer already unifies it with "%").
